title: Architecture-aware autotune manifests for composite kernel families
creator: Aisha Fernandez
description:
Summary:
Create an architecture-aware autotune manifest and publishing workflow that produces deterministic, version-pinned compilation artifacts and performance profiles for composite kernel families (standard MHA, grouped-query-attention (GQA), and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)). This ticket defines the manifest schema, autotune heuristics, scoring metrics, and the staged publishing flow used by model-onboarding to ensure safe rollouts across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Background & Motivation:
- We onboard increasingly diverse model variants (MHA, GQA, MoE) that require different kernel implementations and memory layouts. Current manual tuning is error-prone and slow.
- Need deterministic, auditable artifacts (compile bundles + profile) that can be pinned per-model/version and rolled out with canary and fallback policies.
- Telemetry must capture perf regressions (p50/p95 latency, throughput (tokens/s), peak GPU memory) relative to baseline and enable automated rollback triggers.

Goals:
1) Define a machine-readable autotune manifest that describes: model fingerprint fields, input sequence distribution hints, kernel family choices, compile flags, expected resource envelopes, and stability thresholds.
2) Implement an autotune pipeline that generates: compile bundle (artifact ID), runtime dispatch hints (preferred kernels), and a performance profile with standardized metrics and CI test vectors.
3) Wire publishing: manifest + artifacts -> profile registry with immutability and version pin semantics; provide a pin/unpin API for onboarding.
4) Add safety: staged rollout configuration, canary traffic gates, and automatic fallback to compatible kernel variants if SLOs break.

Acceptance criteria:
- Manifest schema documented in Confluence and validated by unit tests.
- Autotune pipeline produces artifacts reproducibly given the same fingerprint + seed.
- Performance profile schema includes: sample latency p50/p95, throughput tokens/s, memory peak, compile-time, and a histogram of sequence-length buckets.
- Publishing creates an immutable release ID (e.g., kernel-manifest:v2026-03-10+sha) and appears in the profile registry UI.
- Canary rollout can be configured per-customer and will auto-disable if regression > 10% p95 or memory oversubscription > 8%.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (spec, tests) (week 1): Draft manifest schema; add unit tests to validate fields; add example manifests for three sample models (mha-base, gqa-med, moe-8e).
- Phase 2 (autotune pipeline) (weeks 2–3): Implement tuning worker that runs short microbenchmarks (token lengths 8/64/256), collects metrics, and emits compile bundle + profile JSON. Uses deterministic random seed to ensure reproducibility.
- Phase 3 (registry + pinning API) (week 4): Extend profile registry to accept manifests and artifacts; add pin API that maps model:version -> manifest-release-id; include immutability and audit metadata.
- Phase 4 (rollout + telemetry) (weeks 5–6): Integrate canary gate with routing layer, bake rollback logic in runtime to detect SLO drift and revert to previous pin.

Telemetry & CI:
- Add structured telemetry events: autotune.run.{start,complete,fail}, profile.publish, profile.rollback, canary.gate.pass/fail.
- CI microbench jobs run on PRs to validate no regressions in baseline models (mha/gqa/moe).

QA & Test Plan:
- Regression harness against baseline workloads (open datasets) with synthetic and real request traces.
- Canary test: route 5% traffic for 6 hours to new manifest and run SLO checks; percentage/time configurable.
- Data collection: store microbenchmark traces + raw kernel metrics for 14 days.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Non-deterministic compile output across driver/kernel versions: mitigate by including host fingerprint and compile toolchain versions in manifest; mark artifacts incompatible if host fingerprint mismatch.
- Memory overcommit on MoE shards at high sequence lengths: include safety margin in profile and a conservative default canary to validate memory headroom.

Docs & Links:
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RUNTIME/Autotune+Manifest+Spec
- Design notes: https://docs.redwood.com/runtime/autotune-design (internal)
- Example artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/example-autotune-artifacts (internal)
